citation: Grable, J. E., & Lytton, R. H. (1999). Financial risk tolerance revisited: The development of a risk assessment instrument. Financial Services Review, 8(3), 163-181.

items.prompt: In general, how would your best friend describe you as a risk taker?

choices.label: Willing to take risks after completing adequate research

items.prompt: You are on a TV game show and can choose one of the following; which would you take?
You have just finished saving for a once-in-a-lifetime vacation. Three weeks before you plan to leave, you lose your job. You would:

choices.label: Take a much more modest vacation
Go as scheduled, reasoning that you need time to prepare for a job search
Extend your vacation because this might be your last chance to go first-class

items.prompt: If you unexpectedly received $20,000 to invest, what would you do?

choices.label: Deposit it in a bank account, money market account, or insured CD
Invest it in safe high-quality bonds or bond mutual funds
Invest it in stocks or stock mutual funds

items.prompt: In terms of experience, how comfortable are you investing in stocks or stock mutual funds?
When you think of the word "risk", which of the following words comes to mind first?

Some experts are predicting prices of hard assets (gold, jewels, collectibles, real estate) to increase; bond prices may fall, though government bonds are relatively safe. Most of your investment assets are now in high-interest government bonds. What would you do?

choices.label: Sell the bonds; put half into money markets and half into hard assets
Sell the bonds and put the total proceeds into hard assets
Sell the bonds, put all into hard assets, and borrow additional money to buy more

items.prompt: Given the best and worst case returns of the four investment choices below, which would you prefer?

choices.label: $200 gain best case; $0 loss worst case
$800 gain best case; $200 loss worst case
$2,600 gain best case; $800 loss worst case
$4,800 gain best case; $2,400 loss worst case

items.prompt: In addition to whatever you own, you have been given $1,000. You are now asked to choose between:

choices.label: A 50% chance to gain $1,000 and a 50% chance to gain nothing

items.prompt: In addition to whatever you own, you have been given $2,000. You are now asked to choose between:

choices.label: A 50% chance to lose $1,000 and a 50% chance to lose nothing

items.prompt: Suppose a relative left you an inheritance of $100,000, stipulating that you invest ALL the money in ONE of the following choices. Which one would you select?

choices.label: A savings account or money market mutual fund
A mutual fund that owns stocks and bonds
Commodities like gold, silver, and oil

items.prompt: If you had to invest $20,000, which of the following investment choices would you find most appealing?

Your trusted friend, an experienced geologist, is funding an exploratory gold mining venture. It could pay 50–100× if successful, or be worthless (≈20% chance of success). If you had the money, how much would you invest?
